text:
tara: Heads-up — we just got a high-sev from Support: customer reports p99 latency ~3x for a subset of tenants after yesterday's runtime push. Appears cohort-internal (only tenants on runtime-v13.2).

marta: case #INC-24812, reported at 09:12 PST. Customer sample req_id=5f8c9a2e. They say API returns but tails out ~2.2s->6.8s on p99 for generation endpoints.

ben: I'm seeing the same in observability: global p50 stable, p95 ~+10%, p99 tail jump ~x2.8 for workload tag=multi-tenant-synth. Spike started ~02:40 UTC (matches rollout window).

li: Did the rollout touch kernel-scheduler knobs or allocation policy? I remember a change to the tenant allocator in v13.2.

oliver: Yes — v13.2 enabled the new alloc-sweep path by default (reduce fragmentation). It was A/B behind a flag in canary, but yesterday we flipped for all.

ben: Can we bisect quick? If alloc-sweep is suspect, a targeted rollback for that flag for a small cohort might confirm. We should also check KV cache hit rates and batching distribution for affected tenants.

marta: Customer provided a reproducible snippet (their traffic is chatty short prompts). They'll run a synthetic load if we give requests to hit same path. Sample payload: 
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "input": "Summarize: ...",
  "max_tokens": 64
}
```
Request header X-Tenant-ID: tenant-42.

li: Repro steps I propose:
1) Start a small harness hitting tenant-42 with their request mix (short prompts, high QPS).
2) Compare p99 on runtime-v13.1 vs v13.2.
3) Capture heap/alloc metrics and kernel scheduler counters.

tara: If reproduces, hot mitigation options: route tenant-42 to runtime-v13.1 (routing policy override), reduce max-batch-size to limit queueing, temporarily disable alloc-sweep flag. Which is fastest?

ben: Easiest immediate: route to v13.1 via traffic-split config (few min to apply). Config snippet: 
```
api put /routes/tenants/tenant-42/policy
{ "variant": "runtime-v13.1", "pct": 100 }
```
That will cut affected tail quickly.

oliver: Disabling alloc-sweep requires config push to infra but is quick too — however we should be careful: it was meant to reduce fragmentation long-term. Recommend route-first, then revert flag after validation.

marta: I've told customer we can try routing workaround. They asked for ETA. Can we give 20–30m?

ben: If I get thumbs, I'll push routing now and watch p99. @li can you start the synth harness against both variants?

li: Starting harness now. Will post results in 15m.

deploy-bot: deploy v13.1-route-overrides applied to tenant-42 by ben at 02:58:13 UTC.

ben: Route applied. Early signal: p99 dropped from 6.8s -> 1.9s for tenant-42 on first 200 samples. Monitoring now.

marta: Customer confirmed improved UX, reduced complaint severity. They left the session saying they can validate from their side.

li: Harness results:
- runtime-v13.2 p99 ~6.7s
- runtime-v13.1 p99 ~1.8s
Captured alloc churn spike on v13.2 hosts concurrent with requests. Kernel scheduler wait/steal counters slightly elevated.

ben: Root cause hypothesis: new alloc-sweep path increases allocation latency under certain short-prompt high-concurrency patterns, causing long-tail queuing/kicking the slow-path. We'll open a postmortem and plan: revert alloc-sweep default, add a canary with traffic shaping, add microbench for alloc path.

tara: Action items:
- ben: keep route override until we ship a safe fix (owner).
- oliver: prepare a revert PR/flag flip for alloc-sweep (owner).
- li: build microbench to reproduce alloc latency and add to perf suite (owner).
- marta: close the support loop and update customer with timeline (owner).

marta: I'll file follow-up in the ticket and request customer to keep us updated if they see anything else. :thumbsup:

ben: I'll start the rollback plan and coordinate with infra for a staged re-enable once fixed.

tara: Thanks all — great triage. We'll document details in the postmortem once we have binary traces and PRs.
